messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx error rate observed for inference-api (service-tag: inference-api-prod) in us-west-2c. Grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/ai/latency-5xx?s=5186543200

pagerduty: Triggered PD #INC-2026-483. Escalation: mia -> devin

mia: acked the page, en route. I'm oncall for infra. Starting triage.

devin: I'm online. quick check: are we seeing ELB 5xx (gateway) or application 5xx?

mia: ELB target 502/504 spike and app 5xx on a subset of hosts in us-west-2c. CPU fine, but kernel retransmit counters up on those instances.

sudhir: looking at route53 health checks now. I see a weight shift event from route53 replication logs around 5186543105 -> some edge proxies moved traffic to us-west-2c unexpectedly. Investigating why weight changed. Link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/route53/home?#/hostedzone/Z99XXXX

katie: customer impact: we have 3 big customers seeing request failures and retries. UX team reports streaming sessions drop at ~12:05 UTC. Notified CSE to prepare comms.

seb: running quick ELB describe-target-health:
```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:...
# output: many targets unhealthy with "Connection timed out" and some "5xx from target"
```

ops-runner: checked EBS metrics on the affected AZ: average io latency on a few inference nodes spiked to 250ms, IOPS burst limit hit on gp3s. Some instances show EBS ioqueue saturation.

mia: ok that matches kernel retransmits + EBS latency. initial hypothesis: storage path latency in us-west-2c causing app processes to stall and ELB healthchecks to fail -> Route53/edge weight algorithm moved traffic oddly.

devin: can we divert user traffic away from us-west-2c while we isolate? options: 1) route53 weighted traffic change, 2) disable targets in ELB for that AZ, 3) enable cross-region fallback. Which is lowest blast radius?

sudhir: safest immediate: increase Route53 weight for us-west-2a/b and reduce weight for 2c to 0 for the service record. Doing a staged r53 change to avoid flapping. I'll prepare a change-batch.

katie: +1 for staged r53 weight shift. CSE: start drafting status update v1: "Experiencing increased errors in US-WEST-2 (AZ C). We're shifting traffic to healthy AZs while we investigate."

seb: posted runbook snippet for R53 weight change:
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z99XXXX --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.com","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"us-west-2c","Weight":0,"TTL":10}}]}'
```

incident-bot: automation: created a change request draft in /ops/incidents/5186543210/r53-change.json (review required)

mia: I'm going to detach the ELB targets in us-west-2c as a quicker kill-switch if R53 takes time. I'll mark them draining after weights start moving.

devin: FYI if EBS is saturated we should avoid bouncing instances too aggressively; might worsen io pressure on shared storage devices. Prefer R53 first.

ops-runner: applied staged R53 weight change: us-west-2c weight set to 0, us-west-2a/2b increased proportionally. TTL 10s. Change id: CAAA111222.

seb: seeing traffic shift in real-time on Grafana: 2c inbound drops ~95% in last 30s, 5xx rate across service down from 18% to 2%. Latency normalizing.

katie: sent initial customer notice to affected accounts. CSE monitoring for new escalations.

sudhir: opened AWS support case with EBS logs and attached instance IDs. request id SR-0A12B3C4 (high priority).

mia: handing off primary page to devin for deeper storage/network forensics. I'll stay in the channel for comms and postmortem notes. devin, you're P1 owner now. @oncall-bot update: handoff complete.

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded. New primary: devin. Secondary: mia.

devin: confirmed. next steps: run bcc/traceroute from affected hosts to backend endpoints, capture per-instance iostat and blktrace, check for NVMe errors in dmesg, check host ENI retransmit stats.

seb: sample dmesg from i-0abc1234: "nvme0: I/O 12345 timeout, aborting" and kernel: "blk_update_request: I/O error". NVMe controller resets observed.

ops-runner: collecting blktrace from 3 hosts and shipping to s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/5186543210/ for postmortem.

sudhir: AWS replied on SR: "Investigating host-level EBS performance degradation in us-west-2c. We see noisy neighbor IO saturation on host nodes. Mitigating by moving volumes to different placement groups." They requested list of volumes; provided.

devin: good. mitigation plan: keep R53 weights at new state for now, cordon and replace affected instances gradually (we'll use instance replacement to move volumes away from noisy hosts). We'll avoid mass reboot to reduce EBS storm.

mia: customers stable per monitoring; escalation closed for now. PD incident status -> acknowledged -> active mitigation.

katie: timeline note: 12:03 UTC detection (route53/edge weight anomaly), 12:07 UTC R53 weight change executed, 12:09 UTC 5xx reduced under 3%.

seb: action items captured in /ops/incidents/5186543210/actions.md:
- continue instance replacements in us-west-2c (ops)
- request AWS confirmation on noisy neighbor mitigation (sudhir)
- runbook update: consider EBS noisy neighbor appendix (devin)
- postmortem owner: mia

incident-bot: Closing the active page in PagerDuty (INC-2026-483) at 5186544199. Please file postmortem within 72h.

mia: thanks team. I'll draft postmortem and include R53 playbook and EBS noisy-neighbor steps. Leaving channel but monitoring.

devin: leaving detailed forensics notes in the incident artifacts. Good job on quick weight shift.

katie: prepping customer follow-up template.

seb: marking channel for postmortem. Reactions: :thumbsup: :coffee:
